text: Using the SVD W = U*Sigma*V-dagger, how is a general (non-unitary) matrix realized in an MZI processor?
choices: By a single unitary mesh, since every matrix is unitary
As mesh (V-dagger) then diagonal attenuators (Sigma) then mesh (U), with singular values normalized by sigma_max and the global scale restored electronically
By inserting optical amplifiers between MZIs to realize singular values greater than 1
By running one mesh backward to invert the matrix
explanation: SVD factors W into two unitary meshes and a diagonal scaling stage; because passive optics cannot amplify, singular values are normalized by sigma_max (attenuation only) and the overall scale is restored in electronics. Not every matrix is unitary (option 0), passive meshes provide no gain (option 2), and running a mesh backward yields the transpose/adjoint, not a general W (option 3).
